note: The lift table of the Go probe (lift_go.py): every row cites its clause of the defining reference and states its derivation (spec/proposals/rce-form.md, K4). The SHA-256 of this file is the `table` digest of every lift report the probe writes (Appendix D.8, L5).
reference: The Go Programming Language Specification, language version go1.24 (https://go.dev/ref/spec), and the documentation of the standard library package errors at Go 1.24.7

rows.clause: spec: Boolean types; The zero value
rows.derivation: both are the two truth values; Go's zero value of bool is false

rows.clause: spec: Numeric types; The zero value
rows.derivation: int64 is the set of all signed 64-bit integers, as i64 is; the zero value is 0

rows.clause: spec: Numeric types (int is 32 or 64 bits); The zero value
rows.derivation: on the oracle's target, x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu (lang/go1.24/oracle), int is 64 bits, so it is i64; the zero value is 0

rows.clause: spec: Numeric types; The zero value
rows.derivation: uint64 is the set of all unsigned 64-bit integers, as u64 is; the zero value is 0

rows.clause: spec: String types; The zero value
rows.derivation: the probe carries only string fields that are compared or assigned whole, where a sequence of bytes and RCE text agree; the zero value is the empty string

rows.clause: spec: Numeric types (IEEE 754 64-bit); The zero value
rows.derivation: both are IEEE 754 binary64; the zero value is positive zero
a struct value is its fields; each field becomes a region of the state with its type's zero value, the value a Go struct starts with

rows.clause: package errors, func New: each call returns a distinct error value
rows.derivation: distinct error values, compared by identity, are distinct declared errors

rows.rce: event Name; step T on Name
rows.derivation: a pointer-receiver method without parameters changes the receiver and returns an error or nil: one event of the state

rows.rce: step T on Name if c / fail X
rows.derivation: before any write the receiver is unchanged, so returning ErrX when c holds is a step that fails with X and keeps the state (L-GO-ORDER rejects a guard after a write)
assigning a field of the receiver through the pointer changes that region of the state
returning nil as the last statement is the step's normal end
a selector of the receiver reads that region of the state
a parenthesized expression is its operand

rows.clause: spec: Boolean types (the predeclared constants true and false)
rows.derivation: the same two truth values

rows.go: a decimal integer literal without leading zeros
rows.derivation: a decimal literal denotes the same integer in both; octal, hexadecimal and binary forms are not carried (L-GO-EXPR)

rows.go: an interpreted string literal without escapes
rows.derivation: without escapes, the literal's bytes are its UTF-8 text in both
!x is not x
conditional and: the right operand is evaluated only when the left is true, as RCE's and; the probe's operands have no effects
conditional or, as RCE's or; the probe's operands have no effects
equality of values of one comparable type
the negation of ==
the order of integers, of floats (IEEE 754) and of strings by bytes
as <
as <
as <

facts.int_overflow: wraps (Go spec: 'integer overflow ... wraps around'); RCE traps: integer arithmetic requires change (L-GO-INT)
facts.division: truncates toward zero, remainder takes dividend sign (Go spec) = RCE 6.3
facts.error_return: a function returning a non-nil error = an event whose step keeps the state (T8: state unchanged only if no write preceded the return)

rules.L-GO-IMPORT: an import other than "errors": the standard library and other packages are not lifted
rules.L-GO-FUNC: a function declaration or function literal: only pointer-receiver methods of a lifted struct are events
rules.L-GO-METHOD: a method outside the event shape: a receiver that is not a pointer to a lifted struct, parameters, results other than error, or a second method of one name
rules.L-GO-TYPE: a type declaration that is not a struct, an embedded field, or a field type outside the semantics table
rules.L-GO-DECL: a const or var declaration other than `var ErrX = errors.New("Name")`
rules.L-GO-FOR: a for loop (loops and their count bounds are not lifted)
rules.L-GO-SWITCH: a switch, type switch or select statement
rules.L-GO-IF: an if statement other than `if <condition> { return ErrX }` with no init statement and no else
rules.L-GO-ORDER: a guard after a field write: Go keeps the write when the method returns an error, an RCE fail keeps the state unchanged
rules.L-GO-RETURN: a return other than `return ErrX` of a declared error in a guard or `return nil` as the last statement
rules.L-GO-ASSIGN: an assignment other than `recv.field = <expression>` to a field of the receiver
rules.L-GO-CALL: a call (library and user functions are not lifted)
rules.L-GO-COLLECTION: an array, slice, map or channel type, a composite literal, an index or a slice expression
rules.L-GO-POINTER: a pointer type, an address-of or a dereference outside the receiver
rules.L-GO-INT: integer arithmetic: Go's integer overflow wraps, RCE's traps
rules.L-GO-NAME: a Go name that is an RCE keyword, or an error message that is not an RCE name
rules.L-GO-EXPR: another expression form outside the table (named in the reason)
rules.L-GO-STMT: another statement form outside the scope (named in the reason)
